reachPrompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: one complete cat sprite for anatomically natural whole-body animation.
Input image is the CAT IDENTITY ONLY: the same stocky adult brown mackerel tabby with olive-green eyes, pale chin and ringed tail. Create ONE full-body cat in a candid natural vertical scratching posture, three-quarter right-side view. Do not copy its seated pose.
Cat hind feet are flat and bearing weight, hind legs slightly flexed, hips set back, trunk leaning forward diagonally toward the right; the spine has a gentle feline curve rather than standing bolt-upright like a human or meerkat. Both front legs are extended diagonally forward and upward from the natural shoulder girdle, with the two forepaws close together in HEIGHT (about one paw width offset) gripping an INVISIBLE vertical face just right of cat. Head and neck are forward close to paws and the contact area, looking toward the claws (not staring upward at a distant ball); shoulders are forward and upper back stretched. Front paws are ordinary furry CAT paws with curved hooked toes, not human hands/fists. Forelimbs are complete and grow naturally from shoulders, no human-style horizontal biceps+upright forearm L shape. The whole cat should look like it is bracing and exerting force through the spine and hind legs.
Tail extends back and curls lightly near the rear feet. Keep a compact stocky adult cat body, natural head size, correct fur scale and markings; soft realistic lighting.
Full cat including all paw tips, tail and ears completely in view, large padding. Genuinely transparent background; no gradients, room, floor, board, pole, toys, shadows, backdrop, labels, text or watermark. A clean complete isolated cat cutout with actual alpha, not a photo on a colored background.
pullPrompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Edit target: the attached COMPLETE cat cutout. Make ONE neighboring full-body animation key pose of this EXACT same cat during a downward claw-pulling stroke. Preserve cat identity, fur markings, face, camera angle, apparent head size, lighting and transparent background. Keep both rear paws planted at exactly the same positions and keep the original image scale; no zoom, crop or whole-cat translation.
Change the WHOLE posture anatomically: near forepaw grips the invisible vertical face and pulls DOWN about one paw-length; far forepaw stays braced slightly higher. Elbows tuck back toward the cat chest and wrists curl with the grip. Shoulder girdle descends and recoils toward the hips, chest/neck/head lower by about one third of the HEAD HEIGHT, upper back becomes visibly rounder, belly draws inward, haunches sink slightly with flexed hocks while hind feet stay down. Head follows the chest and looks toward the claw contact. It should be a clear compact load-bearing recoil pose after the original long reach, not merely bent arms on the old straight body. Feline forelegs, normal cat paws/claws, no human-arm biceps or fist.
Tail follows the hip a little but preserves its general placement. Keep full paws, claws, tail and ears visible with padding, genuine transparency. No board, floor, room, shadow, gradients, labels or extra cats. One complete connected cat, no separate pieces.
note: Pull image supplies the rendered cat texture; both complete poses supply anatomical geometry. Animation uses a short stroke between 65% and 100% of the pull geometry, not crossfaded photographs.
